questions.questionText: Which molecule is produced directly by transcription of a protein-coding gene?
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase uses a DNA template to synthesize an RNA transcript; translation later uses mRNA to make a polypeptide.

curriculum.objective: Explain and interpret DNA replication, gene expression, mutation and regulation using molecular evidence.

questions.questionText: A DNA template strand reads 3′-TAC GGA-5′. Which mRNA sequence is transcribed?
questions.explanation: RNA is synthesized antiparallel and complementary to the template, replacing thymine pairing with adenine by uracil pairing with adenine.

curriculum.objective: Explain and interpret DNA replication, gene expression, mutation and regulation using molecular evidence.

questions.questionText: A base substitution changes an mRNA codon but not the amino acid encoded. What best explains this result?
options: Every codon can bind any transfer RNA
questions.explanation: Several codons can specify the same amino acid, so some substitutions are silent and do not change the polypeptide sequence.

curriculum.objective: Explain and interpret DNA replication, gene expression, mutation and regulation using molecular evidence.

questions.questionText: In an inducible bacterial operon, lactose is present and glucose is scarce. Which regulatory outcome is most likely?
options: The repressor remains bound and transcription stops
RNA polymerase is destroyed by the inducer
The repressor is inactivated and an activator promotes high transcription
questions.correctAnswer: The repressor is inactivated and an activator promotes high transcription
questions.explanation: Lactose-derived inducer removes repression, while scarce glucose raises cAMP so the activator helps recruit RNA polymerase, producing strong transcription.

curriculum.objective: Explain and interpret DNA replication, gene expression, mutation and regulation using molecular evidence.

questions.questionText: What is an allele?
options: An alternative form of a gene
A protein made by a ribosome
questions.correctAnswer: An alternative form of a gene
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative DNA versions of the same gene found at the same locus on homologous chromosomes.

curriculum.objective: Apply inheritance models and biotechnology techniques to predict outcomes and evaluate genetic evidence.

questions.questionText: For independently assorting genes, what proportion of offspring from AaBb × aabb are expected to be aabb?
questions.explanation: The probability of aa is 1/2 and of bb is 1/2; independent assortment gives 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

curriculum.objective: Apply inheritance models and biotechnology techniques to predict outcomes and evaluate genetic evidence.

questions.questionText: Which sequence correctly describes one PCR cycle?
questions.explanation: Heat first separates DNA strands, cooling lets primers anneal, and a thermostable polymerase then extends from those primers.

curriculum.objective: Apply inheritance models and biotechnology techniques to predict outcomes and evaluate genetic evidence.

questions.questionText: Two linked genes show 12% recombination in a test cross. What percentage is expected for each parental phenotype class?
questions.explanation: Recombinant classes total 12%, leaving 88% parental offspring. The two reciprocal parental classes are expected equally, so each is 44%.

curriculum.objective: Apply inheritance models and biotechnology techniques to predict outcomes and evaluate genetic evidence.

questions.questionText: What is the normal effect of insulin on blood glucose concentration?
options: It converts glycogen directly into glucose
It promotes glucose uptake and storage
questions.correctAnswer: It promotes glucose uptake and storage
questions.explanation: Insulin lowers blood glucose by increasing uptake in responsive cells and promoting conversion of glucose to glycogen and other stores.

curriculum.objective: Analyse nervous, hormonal and excretory control systems to explain coordinated responses and homeostatic regulation.

questions.questionText: What directly causes the rapid depolarisation phase of a neuronal action potential?
options: Potassium ions diffuse into the axon
Chloride ions leave through ligand-gated channels
Voltage-gated sodium channels open and Na⁺ enters
questions.correctAnswer: Voltage-gated sodium channels open and Na⁺ enters
questions.explanation: Once threshold is reached, voltage-gated sodium channels open; sodium influx makes the membrane potential rapidly more positive.

curriculum.objective: Analyse nervous, hormonal and excretory control systems to explain coordinated responses and homeostatic regulation.

questions.questionText: How does antidiuretic hormone reduce water loss in urine?
options: It increases aquaporin insertion in collecting-duct cells
It prevents sodium reabsorption in the loop of Henle
questions.correctAnswer: It increases aquaporin insertion in collecting-duct cells
questions.explanation: ADH makes the collecting duct more permeable to water by promoting aquaporin insertion, increasing water reabsorption into the blood.

curriculum.objective: Analyse nervous, hormonal and excretory control systems to explain coordinated responses and homeostatic regulation.

questions.questionText: Why can glucose appear in urine when blood glucose becomes extremely high?
options: Glucose molecules become too small for filtration
Filtered glucose exceeds the transport maximum for reabsorption
The collecting duct actively secretes all glucose
ADH converts excess glycogen to glucose
questions.correctAnswer: Filtered glucose exceeds the transport maximum for reabsorption
questions.explanation: Carrier proteins in the proximal tubule have a finite transport maximum; above the renal threshold, not all filtered glucose can be reabsorbed.

curriculum.objective: Analyse nervous, hormonal and excretory control systems to explain coordinated responses and homeostatic regulation.

questions.questionText: Which condition distinguishes primary succession from secondary succession?
options: The final community contains no competitors
The process begins on a surface without developed soil
questions.correctAnswer: The process begins on a surface without developed soil
questions.explanation: Primary succession starts where a biological community and developed soil are absent, such as newly exposed rock.

curriculum.objective: Use population, ecological and evolutionary evidence to explain change and evaluate conservation or management decisions.

questions.questionText: In a Hardy–Weinberg population, allele frequencies are p = 0.70 and q = 0.30. What is the expected heterozygote frequency?
questions.explanation: The heterozygote frequency is 2pq = 2 × 0.70 × 0.30 = 0.42.

curriculum.objective: Use population, ecological and evolutionary evidence to explain change and evaluate conservation or management decisions.

questions.questionText: Why can antibiotic-resistant bacteria become more common after antibiotic treatment?
options: Antibiotics direct every bacterium to make the same mutation
Resistant variants survive and leave a greater proportion of descendants
questions.correctAnswer: Resistant variants survive and leave a greater proportion of descendants
questions.explanation: Treatment is a selection pressure: resistant variants have higher survival and reproductive success, increasing resistance-allele frequency.

curriculum.objective: Use population, ecological and evolutionary evidence to explain change and evaluate conservation or management decisions.

questions.questionText: Researchers mark 80 animals. Later they capture 100 animals, including 20 marked individuals. Assuming the method's conditions are met, what is the estimated population size?
questions.explanation: The Lincoln estimate is first sample × second sample ÷ marked recaptures: 80 × 100 ÷ 20 = 400.

curriculum.objective: Use population, ecological and evolutionary evidence to explain change and evaluate conservation or management decisions.

questions.questionText: What is a controlled variable in an experiment?
options: A factor kept constant so it does not confound the result
Any observation that supports the hypothesis
questions.correctAnswer: A factor kept constant so it does not confound the result
questions.explanation: Controlled variables are held constant so differences in the dependent variable can be attributed more confidently to the independent variable.

curriculum.objective: Design, interpret and evaluate biological investigations using controls, sampling, statistics and uncertainty.

questions.questionText: Which test is commonly used to compare observed categorical frequencies with frequencies expected under a hypothesis?
questions.explanation: A chi-squared test evaluates whether differences between observed and expected categorical counts are larger than expected by chance.

curriculum.objective: Design, interpret and evaluate biological investigations using controls, sampling, statistics and uncertainty.

questions.questionText: Why are independent repeats used when measuring enzyme activity?
options: They guarantee the hypothesis is correct
They reveal variability and reduce the influence of random error
They make a control treatment unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: They reveal variability and reduce the influence of random error
questions.explanation: Replicates show biological or measurement variation and allow a more reliable mean, reducing the effect of anomalous random results.

curriculum.objective: Design, interpret and evaluate biological investigations using controls, sampling, statistics and uncertainty.

questions.questionText: A light experiment tests 20 leaves, but every leaf comes from the same plant. Which redesign best addresses pseudoreplication?
options: Measure the same leaves more frequently
Increase light intensity for that plant
Sample comparable leaves from several independently grown plants per treatment
questions.correctAnswer: Sample comparable leaves from several independently grown plants per treatment
questions.explanation: Leaves from one plant are subsamples, not independent biological replicates. Using several plants per treatment captures between-organism variation and supports valid inference.

curriculum.objective: Design, interpret and evaluate biological investigations using controls, sampling, statistics and uncertainty.
